verified_key_information_units.information: Group revenue increased to EUR 1.837 billion in 2025 (from EUR 1.372 billion in 2024), with EBITDA rising to EUR 228 million (from EUR 145 million) and net profit of EUR 69.9 million (from EUR 193.7 million). Total assets grew to EUR 2.597 billion with equity at EUR 1.175 billion.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key Figures of 2025 section, Management Report Overview

candidate_sentences.text: Group revenue increased 33.9% to EUR 1.837 billion from EUR 1.372 billion, while EBITDA rose 56.9% to EUR 227.9 million from EUR 145.3 million.
Net profit fell 63.9% to EUR 69.9 million, while profit attributable to the parent decreased to EUR 70.6 million from EUR 191.3 million.
Total assets decreased 4.4% to EUR 2.597 billion, while equity increased to EUR 1.175 billion from EUR 1.166 billion, lifting the equity ratio to 45% from 43%.

verified_key_information_units.information: The revenue and EBITDA growth was primarily driven by the full-year consolidation of Tallink Grupp (acquired in August 2024), improved performance at Elenger Grupp, and contributions from newly consolidated agriculture assets including Estonia Farmid and Halinga.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key Figures of 2025 commentary, Events in 2025 (Tallink, Energy, Agriculture sections)

candidate_sentences.text: The results benefited from Tallink being consolidated for the full year in 2025, compared with only five months in 2024, as well as an approximately EUR 12 million improvement in Elenger’s EBITDA and contributions from the newly consolidated Estonia Farmid and Halinga businesses.

verified_key_information_units.information: The maritime transport segment carried 5.53 million passengers (0.9% decrease YoY), with cargo units down 19.2% to 245,004 and passenger vehicles down 2.2% to 760,473. Vessel chartering balanced seasonal revenue fluctuations, and technical upgrades focused on reducing CO₂ emissions.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Events in 2025 - Maritime transport business segment

candidate_sentences.text: Tallink carried 5.53 million passengers, down 0.9% year on year; cargo volumes declined 19.2% and passenger vehicles 2.2%.

verified_key_information_units.information: The energy segment delivered 18 TWh of LNG to Inkoo and Klaipėda terminals (unchanged YoY) with a market share of approximately 25% in the Finnish-Baltic region. Investments included a new 4.9 MW solar plant in Latvia and an 8 MWh battery storage facility, with plans for additional storage in Estonia.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Events in 2025 - Energy business segment, Management Report Overview

candidate_sentences.text: In energy, regional gas consumption fell 9% to 39.7 TWh, although Elenger delivered 18 TWh of LNG cargoes, maintaining an approximately one-quarter market share in the Finland–Baltic region.

verified_key_information_units.information: Real estate developments included completion of the 25,000 m² Rimi logistics centre in Laagri and commencement of construction for a 30,000 m² Depo DIY retail space in Lasnamäe. INF Infra secured a EUR 67.2 million contract for Rail Baltica mainline construction on the Kangru-Saku section.
Infortar acquired Estonia Farmid OÜ, gaining control of a major dairy farming and cereals operation, expanding its agriculture segment with the transaction completed on 7 July 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Events in 2025 - Changes in Infortar's supporting sectors (agriculture acquisition details)

candidate_sentences.text: The results benefited from Tallink being consolidated for the full year in 2025, compared with only five months in 2024, as well as an approximately EUR 12 million improvement in Elenger’s EBITDA and contributions from the newly consolidated Estonia Farmid and Halinga businesses.

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity improved to EUR 219.8 million (from EUR 167.6 million) with loan liabilities decreasing to EUR 1.071 billion (from EUR 1.223 billion). The net debt/EBITDA ratio improved to 3.7 (from 4.0). Dividends increased to EUR 62 million (EUR 3 per share) and a share buyback programme repurchased 16,988 shares in Q4 2025.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key Figures of 2025, Share and shareholders section

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets decreased 4.4% to EUR 2.597 billion, while equity increased to EUR 1.175 billion from EUR 1.166 billion, lifting the equity ratio to 45% from 43%.
Interest-bearing liabilities declined 12.4% to EUR 1.071 billion and net debt fell 19.3% to EUR 851.6 million; net debt to EBITDA improved to 3.7 from 4.0.
Operating cash flow increased substantially to EUR 384.0 million from EUR 89.3 million, and cash rose to EUR 219.8 million.
The Group paid EUR 62 million in dividends, or EUR 3 per share, and proposed a 2025 dividend of EUR 3.02 per share.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic initiatives focused on portfolio diversification, particularly expanding into agriculture and renewable energy, with investments in biomethane production and solar power to enhance long-term resilience and align with climate goals.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Letter from the CEO, Events in 2025 (agriculture acquisitions, renewable investments)

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K6, and K7 are fully represented with supporting sentences. K5 is missing entirely—no mention of real estate developments or INF Infra’s Rail Baltica contract. K8 is also missing—no discussion of strategic initiatives around agriculture, renewable energy, biomethane, or solar investments. The summary captures most financial and operational highlights but omits two HIGH-importance strategic and real-estate items, placing it in the 'Generally yes' category.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. It consistently explains the decline in net profit through the impact of one-off gains from Tallink's initial consolidation in 2024 (S1, S5, S6, S8). All financial metrics show logical relationships: revenue and EBITDA growth are supported by full-year consolidation of Tallink and new businesses (S2, S4), while operating profit increase aligns with improved EBITDA margin (S3). The summary clearly links passenger/cargo volume declines to external factors (S10, S11), and financial position improvements are logically presented through asset/liability changes and cash flow growth (S14-S17). There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. All relationships between figures and explanations are internally consistent.
